skill.name: p2p-networking
skill.description: Rust peer-to-peer networking patterns for decentralized repository collaboration with commonware concepts.
skill.summary: Guide Rust P2P message flow, peer management, gossip, sync, and network configuration patterns.
skill.author: AbdelStark

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline crate names, Rust examples, and diagram syntax. One real issue remains: the default configuration binds to 0.0.0.0:9000 and can expose copied P2P services broadly. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Use 127.0.0.1 for local examples, or require users to explicitly choose 0.0.0.0 for public nodes.
Add concrete checks for rate limits, message validation, peer scoring, and key storage before production use.

static_findings.snippet: The `commonware-p2p` crate provides authenticated, encrypted peer communication.

content.value_statement: Decentralized applications need secure peer communication and repository sync. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rust P2P patterns with commonware.
actual_capabilities: Defines Rust message types for handshake, repository sync, gossip, and keep-alive flows.
Outlines peer connection, handshake, peer state, and broadcast patterns.
Shows gossip broadcast, fanout selection, and duplicate message handling.
Describes repository synchronization through ref comparison and missing object fetches.
Provides network configuration fields for listen address, bootstrap nodes, timeouts, limits, and keypair setup.
limitations: Provides patterns and snippets, not a complete runnable crate.
Assumes commonware and project-specific Rust types already exist.
Does not implement NAT traversal, DHT discovery, or bootstrap node operations.
Lists security controls at a high level and still needs production review.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Rust P2P Layer
use_cases.description: Use the message, peer, and configuration patterns to plan a decentralized networking module.

use_cases.title: Plan Repository Sync
use_cases.description: Map how peers exchange refs, detect missing objects, and store fetched repository data.

use_cases.title: Review Network Safety
use_cases.description: Ask an AI assistant to inspect listen addresses, peer authentication, rate limits, and message validation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the P2P Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the handshake, repository sync, gossip, and keep-alive messages in this skill. Keep the answer concise and implementation focused.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Peer Manager
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Rust peer manager using the patterns in this skill. Include connection setup, peer state, broadcasts, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Gossip Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the gossip protocol pattern for duplicate handling, fanout, validation, and denial-of-service risks. Recommend concrete improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Hardening
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production hardening plan for this P2P design. Cover identity keys, listen addresses, bootstrapping, rate limits, and observability.

output_examples.input: Plan repository synchronization for a decentralized code collaboration node.
output: Identify peers that advertise the repository.
Fetch missing objects from selected peers.
Validate objects before storing them locally.

output_examples.input: Review the default network configuration for deployment risk.
output_examples.output: The main risk is the public listen address. Use a local bind for development and require explicit public exposure for production nodes.

output_examples.input: Explain how gossip duplicate handling works.
output_examples.output: Each message gets a content-derived identifier. Seen identifiers are skipped, while new messages are processed and rebroadcast to selected peers.

best_practices: Treat all peer messages as untrusted until authenticated and validated.
Use explicit listen addresses and document when public binding is required.
Add rate limiting, peer scoring, and observability before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not bind public interfaces by default in examples meant for local development.
Do not process gossip data before validating size, topic, and schema.
Do not store fetched repository objects without integrity checks.

faq.question: Is this a complete P2P implementation?
faq.answer: No. It is a pattern guide with Rust snippets for message flow, peers, gossip, sync, and configuration.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require commonware?
faq.answer: The guidance references commonware concepts and crates, but target projects must supply the actual dependencies and types.

faq.question: Is the default listen address safe?
faq.answer: The example uses 0.0.0.0:9000, which exposes all interfaces. Prefer a local address unless public access is intended.

faq.question: Does it cover peer discovery?
faq.answer: It mentions DHT and bootstrap nodes, but it does not implement discovery mechanics.

faq.question: What should teams review before production use?
faq.answer: Review identity key storage, message validation, rate limits, peer scoring, public binding, and repository object integrity.
